“I was all alone in the bar when two passers-by suddenly appeared. They pointed to the bottles of alcohol behind the bar, then one of them told me in Arabic: ‘You should be ashamed of yourself serving alcohol in the Ramadan period.’

The waitress said one of the two men then shouted: “If I was God, I would have hung you.”

Unfazed by his threatening behaviour, the waitress shot back: “You’re not God to judge me.”

It shows that i’m not mass producing and have the extra time to write something on every bag. The hang tag is easily removable and can be kept for later reference.

As of right now I am selling to farmer’s markets and a local coffee shops. I know this packaging isn’t retail friendly and I will require a revision once these beans hit a larger audience, but for now this is a cost effective and simple approach.

New Tags Here are the updated tags. These tags have dropped the ‘processing’ subtitle and replaced it with ‘roast level’. I am easily able to change the colored banner to identify different roasts.

I like the graphic design, nice and clean with a good amount of character.

Couple of thoughts:

  • Somewhere on the packaging should designate that its whole bean (assuming it is) and also how much coffee is in the bag - oz or grams.

  • The new tags don't have quite as much character, the droplet icon was a nice touch.

  • On an ease of use and storage note, are you sure you want to go with the hang tag approach? I only ask because you want your packaging to have maximum visibility throughout its life-cycle, the current design means most customers will look at before purchase but take off when in use, as the hang tag would get annoying for people that open and close the bag many times (small or manual grinder users).

I would like to move towards either stickers, printed bags, or stamps in the future, but for now the tags are what I can afford. I was hoping that when they take off the tag they will keep it as a reference in case they want to order more later on.
